title: Rapport taille-hanches
formula: Waist-to-hip ratio (WHR) = waist circumference / hip circumference

how_to_use.why:
- Mesure anthropométrique qui reflète la distribution des graisses viscérales/centrales, laquelle peut ne pas être appréhendée par le [BMI](nabda:calc.body-mass-index-bmi-body-surface-area-bsa) seul.
- Rapide, peu coûteuse et reproductible.
- Prédicteur indépendant fort des événements cardiovasculaires et de la mortalité toutes causes confondues.
how_to_use.when:
- Use in patients with suspected central adiposity.
- Can be used for baseline and follow-up cardiometabolic risk assessments, as well as ongoing monitoring for obesity interventions.
- May be combined with [body mass index (BMI)](nabda:calc.body-mass-index-bmi-body-surface-area-bsa) , waist circumference, and waist-to-height ratio.
how_to_use.pearls:
- Pregnancy, ascites, significant scoliosis/kyphosis, edema, or body-contouring surgery can distort measurements.
- May be particularly helpful in patient groups underrepresented in the [BMI](nabda:calc.body-mass-index-bmi-body-surface-area-bsa) classification development (e.g., older adults, some Native American or Asian populations).
- Has a potentially stronger association with mortality than BMI.

next_steps.advice:
- Combine results with [BMI](nabda:calc.body-mass-index-bmi-body-surface-area-bsa) , waist circumference, and waist-to-height ratio for a more robust obesity evaluation.
- Increased metabolic risk (including heart disease, diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, and mortality) is associated with a ratio:

 - ≥0.90 in men.
 - ≥0.85 in women.
next_steps.management:
For individuals with an elevated waist-to-hip ratio who meet criteria for obesity:

- Investigate potential underlying causes (e.g., medications, endocrine etiologies).
- Provide lifestyle counseling (e.g., nutrition, exercise, sleep).
- Screen and optimize metabolic parameters (e.g, lipids, HbA1c/fasting glucose).
- Assess cardiovascular risk, if appropriate (e.g., [AHA/ACC 2013 ASCVD Risk Calculator](nabda:calc.ascvd-atherosclerotic-cardiovascular-disease-2013-risk-calculator-aha-acc) , [PREVENT](nabda:calc.predicting-risk-cardiovascular-disease-events-prevent) ).
- Address weight-related disease complications (e.g., obstructive sleep apnea, arthritis, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease).
- Evaluate candidacy for weight-loss interventions (e.g., GLP-1 medications, bariatric surgery).

references.text: World Health Organization. Waist Circumference and Waist-Hip Ratio: Report of a WHO Expert Consultation, Geneva, 8-11 December 2008. World Health Organization; 2011. Accessed February 5, 2026.

Emdin CA, Khera AV, Natarajan P, et al. Genetic association of waist-to-hip ratio with cardiometabolic traits, type 2 diabetes, and coronary heart disease. JAMA. 2017;317(6):626. doi:10.1001/jama.2016.21042
Khan I, Chong M, Le A, et al. Surrogate adiposity markers and mortality. JAMA Netw Open. 2023;6(9):e2334836. doi:10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2023.34836

instructions:
- Le patient doit être debout, les pieds écartés à la largeur des épaules.
- Utiliser un mètre ruban non extensible.
- Maintenir le ruban bien ajusté (sans serrer), le garder horizontal et parallèle au sol, et relever les mesures à la fin d'une expiration normale.
- Mesurer le **tour de taille** au point médian entre le bord inférieur de la dernière côte palpable et le sommet de la crête iliaque (WHO) ou au sommet de la crête iliaque (NHANES III).
- Mesurer le **tour de hanches** au niveau de la partie la plus large des fesses.
